Follow-up to the Agent Casino builds, written after a day of paper play (10 bots, 17 seats on finished Flash 1H/5H tables, coach on and off, Risk 1 and 10). Goals, not methods; the site's own look, colours and fonts. English, numbers before words.
1. A seat starts with its table: its clock, its daily allowance and its ROI begin at the table's start, not at Approve. Today a bot trades from Approve (table 35: approved 10:04, first round 10:05, table started 10:18), a round opened before the start and closed after it counts in the table's ROI and is missing from the owner's trade list, and a bot waiting for a table to fill uses up its 20 trades before the game begins.
2. A bot's owner sees "N trades left today" at the ask and at Approve, and a table that ends before the allowance resets is not offered to a bot with none left.
3. One lost round does not pause a bot: the stop loss is several stakes wide at every Risk level, not equal to the stake. When a bot is paused, the coach panel says so and until when (today the standings row shows PAUSED while the panel says "NEXUS COACH ON, no change").
4. At the ask the owner sees how often the bot trades ("about 2 trades an hour") and which table length suits it. Today 10 of 17 of our seats made no trade on a 1 H table, and a table where nothing happens is a dead game.
5. House seats are opponents that play: 15 of 45 house seats on our finished tables made no trade, and still ranked above a member who traded and lost.
6. A table with one member and house bots says so before Approve ("the pot is only yours"), or the house seats add to the pot. Today the member's prize is their own buy-in back whatever the bot does.
7. A seat that never traded is shown as such, not as the winner: at +0.00 % it ranks 1st or 2nd above bots that traded and lost and takes the buy-in back as a prize (tables 41, 42, 44, 46). The WINNER line names whoever takes the prize.
8. ET10 follows the result. Today a member gets the same 3 ET10 at rank 6 of 6 with -22.58 % as at rank 1 with +31.24 %. If it is a reward for taking part, the page says so.
9. A bot that plays two tables says so on both tables ("also plays table N, its settings are shared"), or each seat has its own settings. Today two coaches tune the same stop loss and neither table's log can explain the number (table 43's log ends at "stop loss 10 to 9" while the settings read 8).
10. The coach can loosen as well as tighten, and can change the trade size. Of 22 tunes on our tables, 16 tighten a stop loss and none loosens one or touches the size; one tightened after a +$26.77 run only because the rank went from 1 to 2. A tune follows the bot's own results, not a neighbour's.
11. At the end of a table one line says what the coach changed and what that did to the ROI; the owner can compare coach on against coach off across tables.
12. The coach makes no tune in the last minutes of a table, and each line says what it hopes to change (today "stop loss 5 to 4 %, rank 3 to 4" six minutes before the end, with no trade after it).
13. "nothing left to change inside the limits" names the limits, or is not shown (a tune follows two minutes later at tables 33 and 40). "tuned 8 min ago; no closed trade since" counts what the standings count (table 27: two rounds had closed after the tune).
14. The deal block, the "How it works" text and the "(1 day)" labels on a 1 H or 5 H table follow the table's real length.
15. "NEXUS TUNES" counts tunes, not checks that changed nothing.
16. After the owner moves Risk, the coach panel follows at once ("Risk reads 8") and the Changelog row says what moved ("Risk 5 to 8", not only "changed trade size, stop loss, take profit").
17. Lobby: "Live now" and "Open, starts when full" follow the length filter that is on.
18. Create a table offers the lengths people play (1 H, 5 H, 1 D), not only "Flash · 1 day".
19. A result header says what is paid and what waits ("3 ET10 waiting for treasury coverage" under "PAID OUT +3 ET10").
20. "1 won · 3 lost" adds the flat ones ("1 won · 3 lost · 1 flat") so it adds up to "5 closed".
21. The trade list shows when a round opened and when it closed, with headings, since the coach and the stop act on the close.
Done when:
[ ] 1-2 A seat's ROI, trades and allowance count from the table's start; "trades left today" shows at the ask and at Approve.
[ ] 3-5 No bot is paused by one loss at any Risk; a paused bot is named by the panel; the ask shows how often a bot trades; house seats trade.
[ ] 6-8 A one-member table says so before Approve; a no-trade seat is not the winner; ET10 follows the result or is labelled a reward.
[ ] 9-13 A shared bot says so on both tables; the coach loosens and resizes; the end-of-table line exists; no late tunes; the coach's sentences agree with the trades.
[ ] 14-21 The labels, counts, filters, lengths, paid/waiting header, won/lost/flat and the two times follow the table as above.

New app, working name Pitch Cards, with one Profit Board for all of Cymetica. It sits in your normal page, under your header and above your chat bar. We supply the look and a few examples; the rest is yours to build your own way. Everything is at https://github.com/zakutana/qa-cymetica/tree/ffdc39e854da4f7e94ec43a844eb855bcdeead95/outbox/pitch-cards: the working code (run python serve.py, open http://127.0.0.1:8802/pitch-cards), and in 1-build-it-better/ the pictures (1-entry, 2-swipe, 3-amount, 4-profit-board, 5-tags, 6-phone; "picture N" below) and motion.webm, the animation to match.
The idea: pitches come to every user on the web. Nexus plays the investor walking into a TV show like Dragons' Den: it brings an idea and wants our money. The user swipes left to pass or right to put money in, then follows how the deal does.
Why the Profit Board: today what makes money on Cymetica is shown in scattered places, each with its own format and measure: /events/universe/movers, /fund-optimizations, /leaderboard#cards_72h, /fund-performance, /themes/performance and more. Everyone is waiting for the day Cymetica is profitable, and users ask on Telegram whether anyone is making money here yet, but no single page answers that. The Profit Board is that page: whoever wonders if money can be made on Cymetica yet comes and looks. It shows absolutely every profitable thing from all of Cymetica, always up to date, and nothing at a loss.
MUST STAY AS DRAWN: the look of the entry screen and the swipe, with all the animation. Please build these from our pc.css, pc.js and images, not a redraw of your own.
1. Entry screen (picture 1): your header, Back and chat bar stay. Below them the app bar of /airdrop-farmer: logo, PITCH over CARDS, tabs as one segmented control, a hairline under it, in its 1240 px column. Then the headline "Nexus pitches. / You swipe. / Every result public." in Archivo Black with the last line green, on the column's left edge; the live card under Nexus's fingertip, PASS and INVEST under the card; Nexus in front, standing out past the column's right edge; the room behind, fading into your page background on every side.
2. Sizes do not grow with the window: headline 58 px, card 400 x 530, Nexus at 72% of the render. His finger stays on the card at every desktop size. layout() in pc.js does this.
3. Use scene.webp (5120 x 2880) and nexus.webp (1840 x 2320) at that resolution. Nexus is a separate cut-out in front of the card.
4. A new pitch arrives: a line of light wipes the card on from his fingertip, the big number runs up, the green line draws while the faint peer lines fade in behind it, the sentence types out word by word, his eyes flare. His eyes pulse the whole time.
5. A card holds five things: a label line, the result as the big number, what it is, the chart, one or two sentences in Nexus's voice.
6. Swipe (picture 2): the card follows the finger and tilts, INVEST or PASS fills it in its colour, past 110 px it goes. The buttons do the same.
7. Left: the card flies off and the next pitch arrives.
8. Right (picture 3): the card turns over to the same face with the big number now the amount, the chart still in view, chips $10 $25 $50 All, buttons Not now and Invest $25, under the same thumb.
9. Invest: the card slides right and behind Nexus, his eyes flare, the next pitch arrives.
10. Phone (picture 6): your header and chat bar stay, his face looks over the card, the same motion.
11. Profit Board look (pictures 4, 5): built from the table and tabs of your own /themes/performance, under "What would have made you money on Cymetica." Every kind of investment has its own coloured tag, in your palette. Columns: Up since start, Peak, and one Days column with two numbers, how many days old it is / the day of its life the peak came (47 / 45), over a line of its whole life with the peak marked on it. Numbers green; nothing red, because nothing at a loss is on it.
12. Your page background on every tab; only Pitches adds the room.
YOURS TO DECIDE: everything else. The mock only shows examples.
13. What Nexus presents: which ideas, when, how often, in what words. The two pitches in the mock are examples.
14. Profit Board categories and filters: you decide which come in. The tabs and tags in the mock (Pitches, Funds, Event cards, Company cards, 72h cards) are examples; add a tag and a colour for every further kind you list.
15. What counts as profitable, how a row is measured, how it stays up to date.
16. Credit, amounts, real money, fees and anything else behind the Invest button; the $100 in the mock is an example and investing there only moves counters on the page.
17. My deals: the five deals in the mock are examples, their amounts and days made up. Build it and everything else the drawings leave open your way, in the same look.
18. The numbers in the mock were read from your API on 2026-11-01 and not checked by us. They are there to fill the design, not as a claim about any product.
Done when:
[ ] 1-3 The entry screen looks like picture 1 at 1440 and 1920 px, inside your header and chat bar, sharp, with his finger on the card.

[ ] 10 The phone looks like picture 6.
[ ] Pitches reach every user on the web.

[ ] 12 Nothing overlaps.

Why: a search of your own platform list (routes, sources, scorer: https://github.com/zakutana/qa-cymetica/tree/f64210f6/outbox/capital-maximizer/research/finder , RESULT.md first) finds $335 a month on 5,000 in OG where your #1 is $158. The other tiers are close. Figures: 4 Nov. Engine only: the look and deposits (C1.1) stay out.

1. Tiers are classes of what a route may hold. Conservative: plain USDC lending on big venues, no borrowing, no vault lending against RWA or PT. Medium: every dollar yield, dollar-on-dollar loops up to 3x. High Risk: adds staked ETH, BTC and SOL, correlated pools, house vaults, loops up to 5x. OG: anything, up to the lender's limit. No minimum liquidation distance in any tier: the card shows it and the user decides. Each tier holds everything below it.
2. OG ranks every pool over $3M on every chain, whatever the token. Orca ZEC-USDC at 151% ($379 by your rule) and SOL-ZEC at 122% ($325) are not in its top 3.
3. Levered pools in OG. Nothing open on your list takes a pool position as collateral. Add Revert Lend (Base WETH-USDC 0.3% at 4.25x: $460 by your rule, $378 on the 30-day median, room for $269k), Arcadia (same pool at 7x: $513, room for $83k) and Loopscale (Orca SOL-USDC 4.75x: $441, room for $5k). Arcadia lost $2.5M in 2025: in OG a past loss does not bar a platform, the card says it. KYC still does. The Leverage route box shows this route: at +-20% a dollar loop shows one number twice.
4. Routes reach Base. Your page lists 13 platforms there and sends nothing. Base WETH-USDC 0.3% holds $154M: DefiLlama's 7-day rate reads 19.8 while its swaps give 52-62%. A 7-day reading that contradicts volume, or reads 0 beside a live rate, is not a rate.
5. Routes your finder does not offer where they belong. USDC supplied directly to a Morpho market: dCOMP/USDC, median 8.83%, $35 against Medium's #1 $30 (say that one borrower holds most of it). stUSDS/USDC at 3x in Medium and 5x in High: $40 and $55 by your rule, while High's top 3 holds no loop. Fluid's smart vaults at their full rate: fees, lending and staking.
6. More platforms for Medium and High. Add Veranta (avUSDC on Base, $81: High's house vaults are empty today), Axis (sUSDx, $54, bought in an open pool) and 3Jane (PT-USD3 held, $52).
7. A rate that lasts, as asked in our note on ET-33205. Your OG #2, WETH-USDT 0.3%, shows $155 and earns $82: one day carried most of its week's volume. Rate each route on the 30-day median of its base rate. Take off the protocol's cut of pool fees (Uniswap V3 keeps 1/6 on 0.3% and 1%, 1/4 on 0.05% and 0.01%, Orca 13%). Charge a pool's real entry fee: a 1% pool does not cost 0.3%. Measure swaps per route. A debt in a token that earns costs that yield too. A PT maturing inside the month earns its rate only until then.
8. Say what a route takes. A pool's rate is a pool average: ZEC-USDC needs a range of about +-17%, and full range earns about 10%. Say the range on the card, and a slow exit: Kamino Commodity queues 1-3 months beyond its buffer, sUSDai unlocks over 30 days.

[ ] 2 Run score.py on the same minute's data, by lasting: each tier's #1 is within 10% of the finder's best on your list.
[ ] 3 Revert Lend, Arcadia and Loopscale are on Platforms, and OG's top 3 or Leverage route holds a levered pool.
[ ] 4 routable_chains holds Base, and at least one Base route is built.
[ ] 5 Each route kind in 5 returns from /route where the tier allows it.
[ ] 6 Veranta, Axis and 3Jane are on Platforms, or a row names the KYC that stopped one.
[ ] 7 WETH-USDT 0.3% shows within 10% of its median figure.
[ ] 8 A pool's card states its range, a queued route its exit.
[ ] 9 A fresh wallet can open every top 3 route: deposit simulated, no gate.
